## Where to watch wildlife on an eight-country journey

Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Colombia all feature in our [journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). This selection features a tour covering all four countries with opportunities to observe wildlife. The main dedicated wildlife activities take place on the Galápagos Islands in Ecuador. This is not a separate four-country safari: the journey also travels through Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Ecuador.

Within the four selected countries, the most distinctive nature stops are Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and Brazil's Iguazu Falls. Chile adds the Atacama Desert, while Colombia contributes the surroundings of Guatapé and several city stops. If wildlife watching is your priority, it is important to distinguish scheduled animal encounters from the general scenic appeal of the itinerary.

## Bolivia: flamingos, lagoons and salt flats

From [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the itinerary crosses the border into Bolivia. A two-day 4×4 jeep journey begins, visiting Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The last of these is known for its flamingos, which may be seen in their natural habitat when conditions permit. The jeep tour itself focuses on lagoons, geysers and salt flats; it does not promise a separate ornithological excursion.

The following day takes in the Honda, Chiar Khota, Hedionda and Cañapa lagoons, the Chiguana salt flat and the [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) area. These varied high-altitude ecosystems are fascinating in their own right: mineral lakes, volcanic terrain and salt-covered expanses. Sightings of particular bird species cannot be guaranteed at every lake.

The programme notes elevations above 4,000 metres and the possibility of altitude sickness. The stop in [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) also serves as part of the acclimatisation process. Consider the altitude, your health and the overnight stay in an expedition-style hotel in advance. Other itineraries featuring the country's natural sights can be found in the [Bolivia nature tours catalogue](/interests/nature/tours/bolivia/).

## Brazil: Iguazu and an optional bird park visit

In Brazil, the nature-focused section centres on [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The excursion explores the Brazilian side of the falls amid tropical vegetation. Above all, it is an encounter with the waterfalls and surrounding forest.

A visit to [Parque das Aves near Iguazu](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) is offered in this programme **at an additional charge**. The same applies to Macuco Safari, involving travel through the forest and a boat ride towards the falls rather than a dedicated wildlife search. At the bird park, visitors see birds in enclosures, not in the wild. If that experience is a priority, agree on the timing and cost in advance; the standard waterfall excursion does not replace this optional visit.

In Rio, the itinerary visits Corcovado with views over Tijuca Forest. However, the Rio days mainly explore the city's landmarks and do not include a dedicated wildlife search. To explore a different mix of activities, see [wildlife tours in Brazil](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/).

## What Chile offers and how Colombia differs

In Chile, travellers visit Santiago before flying to Calama and continuing to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). This introduces the dry, high-altitude landscapes and prepares the group for the Bolivian section. No dedicated animal-watching activities are specified during the Chilean days. An astronomy excursion is available separately.

The Colombian section includes a trip to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón rock, followed by Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá. The emphasis here is on panoramic scenery, history and urban culture. The itinerary does not include a separate safari or ornithological excursion in Colombia.

Adding Colombia broadens the range of landscapes but also increases the number of flights and city days. If your primary interest is wildlife, assess the time actually spent in suitable natural areas rather than the number of countries visited.

## Comparing the nature experiences before you travel

If you most want to see flamingos, the Bolivian section through Laguna Colorada is the strongest match. If waterfalls and tropical birds interest you, focus on Iguazu and arrange the optional bird park visit. In Chile, the main nature experience is the landscape of the Atacama; in Colombia, it is the scenery around Guatapé.

The complete eight-country tour also visits Ecuador and the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The itinerary includes giant tortoise watching on Santa Cruz and one of two alternative marine excursions featuring birds and marine wildlife; the chosen sea excursion is confirmed after booking. These wildlife activities take place **outside the four countries in this selection**, not in Colombia or Chile.

To compare other combinations of countries, browse [multi-country wildlife itineraries](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/). If waterfalls, mountains and desert landscapes matter more, explore the separate [Nature](/interests/nature/) theme. The [general Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Colombia selection](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_colombia/) shows trips covering these countries without a wildlife-interest filter.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife watching and nature stops

### Are flamingo sightings guaranteed?

No. The itinerary includes Laguna Colorada, where flamingos live, but the presence and behaviour of wild birds depend on natural conditions.

### Is the bird park in Brazil included in the price?

No. The eight-country itinerary lists it as an optional excursion at extra cost. The main tour includes an excursion to the Brazilian side of Iguazu Falls.

### Can I visit only these four countries?

The featured tour covers eight countries. If you would prefer a shorter trip limited to Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Colombia, the order of travel, excursions and price would need to be agreed as a separate itinerary.

## Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador in one journey

This combination offers travellers three very different nature experiences: the waters and forests of [Brazil](/brazil/), the dry high-altitude deserts of [Chile](/chile/) and [Bolivia](/bolivia/), and the volcanic islands of [Ecuador](/ecuador/). But these experiences **do not occur in four consecutive countries**.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. [“Eight South American countries in 32 days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Colombia. First come São Paulo, Rio and Iguazu; later Santiago and the Atacama; then the Bolivian plateau; and, after Peru, Quito, Santa Cruz and other Galápagos islands. To make an informed choice, consider the entire itinerary rather than simply adding up attractions from four country catalogues.

## Brazil: waterfalls and city walks before the Andes

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itinerary visits Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and historic neighbourhoods. After flying to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), travellers visit the Brazilian side of the waterfalls. The next day introduces the Argentine side before the route continues to Buenos Aires.

Expect plenty of walking in warm, humid conditions; spray and wet surfaces are almost unavoidable near the falls. Lightweight clothing, a sealable case for electronic equipment and shoes with non-slip soles will be more useful than elaborate expedition gear. The bird park and the Macuco Safari boat experience are listed as optional activities, so participation depends on a separate choice.

## The Atacama: gateway to Bolivia's highlands

The Chilean section begins in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A flight to Calama followed by a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) opens the mountain-and-desert stage. An optional evening astronomy excursion is possible in suitable conditions; for this tour, availability also depends on the lunar calendar.

After spending the night in the Atacama, the group approaches the land border with Bolivia. Two days in 4×4 vehicles connect Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geothermal area, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). This section includes a night in an expedition hotel, and some stops lie above 4,000 metres. It is no ordinary sightseeing transfer: altitude, wind, cold nights and distance from urban infrastructure call for preparation.

After the salt flat, the itinerary includes a flight from Uyuni to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and a tour of the city. It then enters Peru via Tiwanaku and Desaguadero. **The published itinerary does not include a direct transfer from Bolivia to Ecuador.**

## Ecuador: from high-altitude Quito to the sea and the Galápagos

After Puno, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima in Peru, the group flies to [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), visits the equator line, then flies to the archipelago. On [Santa Cruz Island](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the programme includes a trip to the highlands and accommodation in Puerto Ayora. The sea excursion follows **one of two alternatives**: North Seymour and Bachas Beach, or South Plaza and Cape Carrión. The tour does not promise both routes together.

For the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), a regular flight ticket to Ecuador is not the only requirement. The official procedure involves a TCT transit control card, biosecurity screening of luggage and a conservation fee. Allow time at the mainland Ecuador airport to complete the required steps before boarding the island flight. Uncontrolled imports of food and biological materials are prohibited on the islands, so check these rules before packing.

The transition from Bolivia to the Galápagos brings a dramatic change in temperature, humidity and elevation. In the Andes, warm layers, a windproof jacket and sun protection are useful; on the islands, lightweight clothing, sun protection and items suited to the sea excursion are more appropriate. One large, heavy suitcase packed for every possible activity can be impractical: it makes sense to organise clothing by travel stage and check airline baggage limits.

## Altitude, climate and wellbeing

The main health consideration in this combination arises before Ecuador: altitude sickness can occur when ascending quickly above your usual elevation. For nights on the Altiplano and time around La Paz, discuss contraindications and an acclimatisation plan. The CDC guidance reviewed for this itinerary specifically notes that physical fitness does not guarantee resistance to altitude. If someone becomes unwell, medical safety must take precedence over the travel schedule.

Unlike Bolivia, the Galápagos stage takes place mostly near sea level, but island heat and sunshine present their own physical demands. Adding optional adventure activities simply because you still have energy after Uyuni is unwise: rest days and travel days need to be balanced according to individual needs.

## Passports, money and actual connections

The four selected countries use different currencies: the Brazilian real, Chilean peso, Bolivian boliviano and **the US dollar in Ecuador**. A service price quoted in USD does not mean that local expenses in Chile or Bolivia can always be paid in US dollar notes; check card acceptance and how much reserve cash to carry separately. For travellers using Russian-issued cards, acceptance depends particularly on the issuing bank and payment network.

Entry and transit requirements for Russian passport holders must be checked for the actual travel dates in each country, including transit through Argentina, Uruguay and Peru. Other nationalities require a different assessment. Entering Chile involves declaring plant and animal products under the SAG procedure; the Galápagos have their own biosecurity controls. Standard passport checks and these sanitary measures serve different purposes.

We can discuss the flight sequence, 4×4 transport, border-crossing time and island procedures. Specific services, pricing and changes to the original [32-day journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) are agreed separately.

## Frequently asked questions about Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador

### Is there a direct transfer from Uyuni to the Galápagos?

No. In the published itinerary, Bolivia is followed by Peru, then Quito and a separate flight to the Galápagos. A shorter version would require different flight connections.

### Which is more physically demanding: the waterfalls or the high-altitude lagoons?

The most specific physical challenge is the altitude of the Bolivian Altiplano, where part of the route rises above 4,000 metres. At the waterfalls, the main practical considerations are humidity, walking and slippery surfaces.

### Can I combine Atacama stargazing with both island excursions?

The Atacama astronomy excursion is optional and runs under agreed conditions. In the Galápagos, the itinerary includes one of two alternative sea excursions, so both cannot be promised.

### Do I need special preparations to enter the Galápagos?

Yes. In addition to Ecuadorian entry documents, you need the archipelago's required transit card, luggage biosecurity screening and payment of any applicable fee. Check the requirements before buying flights to the islands.

### What if I want to visit only these four countries?

A new flight sequence and trip duration would have to be designed. This page shows how the four countries fit into the larger eight-country tour; it is not a ready-made, independent four-country programme.

## Where the real adventure begins in this country combination

For Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador, we offer a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It also covers Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Colombia. The four-country combination shown here is therefore a filter on a larger journey, not a standalone expedition visiting only those four countries.

The most demanding active section, involving altitude and long drives over challenging terrain, lies where Chile meets Bolivia. Brazil offers walks to Iguazu Falls, while Ecuador brings land-based and sea excursions in the Galápagos. These involve different kinds of exertion: high-altitude driving, humid tropical conditions and a day at sea call for different preparations.

## Chile and Bolivia: from acclimatisation to 4×4 jeeps

After the sightseeing programme in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the itinerary includes a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The stop also helps travellers adjust before heading into the Bolivian highlands. The optional evening astronomy excursion in the Atacama is not a mandatory part of the itinerary.

The next day, travellers cross the border and begin a two-day 4×4 jeep excursion. The route passes Laguna Verde, the Dalí Desert, the Polques hot springs, the Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). An overnight stay is scheduled in an expedition-style hotel in the desert. The second day combines several high-altitude lagoons, the Chiguana salt flat and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

Here, “adventure” means a genuinely long journey, high elevation and constantly changing scenery. Some highland sections exceed 4,000 metres, where altitude sickness is possible. When preparing, discuss your health, appropriate clothing and tolerance for long drives. Multi-day sporting treks are not included in this programme.

## Brazil: tropical walks without promises of extreme sports

In Brazil, the route visits Rio de Janeiro and [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). A visit to the waterfalls is included, while the bird park and Macuco Safari are offered at additional cost. Their availability and conditions require separate confirmation.

Walking to waterfall viewpoints and sightseeing around Rio differ from the Bolivian jeep expedition. Do not assume that the “Adventure” label means rafting, climbing or strenuous hiking in Brazil. Travellers seeking a more active programme can compare this format with [adventure tours in Brazil](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/).

## Ecuador: islands, a sea excursion and an alternative itinerary

After Peru, the journey continues via Quito to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The programme includes arrival on [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and a visit to the island's highlands, followed by one day of sea excursions.

There are two alternatives: [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) with Bachas Beach **or** [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) with Cape Carrión. The chosen option is confirmed after booking; the programme does not promise both sets of places on the same day. Consider the conditions of the boat journey and landings, the weather and the suitability of the selected route for each traveller.

The Ecuadorian section offers another kind of adventure, but it is quite different from the Bolivian jeep journey. If you are mainly interested in island excursions, compare [adventure itineraries featuring Ecuador](/interests/adventure/tours/ecuador/).

## Combining three different kinds of exertion in one trip

The full itinerary already determines the practical sequence: Brazilian cities and Iguazu first, followed by Chile and Bolivia, and later Peru and Ecuador. City tours, domestic flights and transfers separate the adventure-focused stages. The four selected countries should not be mistaken for one continuous section that can be covered in a single vehicle.

Ask four questions when comparing trips. How many days are actually spent in natural settings? Is a high-altitude route suitable for you? Which Galápagos sea excursion will be confirmed? Which optional activities matter enough to include in your budget and timetable in advance?

Find the details and day-by-day sequence on the [tour page](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Other combinations with the same interest are listed in the [multi-country adventure catalogue](/multi-country/interests/adventure/), while [all itineraries featuring these four countries](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_ecuador/) are available without the thematic filter.

## Frequently asked questions about the adventure section

### Do I need athletic training for Bolivia?

The tour includes jeep journeys across the highlands, not a stated mountaineering route. Nevertheless, elevations above 4,000 metres and road conditions require careful consideration of your health and readiness to travel.

### Are both Galápagos sea excursions included?

No. The programme includes one of two alternatives; the specific option is confirmed after booking.

### Can these four countries be treated as a standalone tour?

No. Our itinerary covers eight countries, and these four form part of its geography. A shorter private version would require a separately agreed route and set of services.

## A historical journey through Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador

Combining four countries lets you discover very different cultural traditions: Brazil's urban life, Santiago's historic centre, Bolivia's pre-Columbian monuments and Ecuador's capital. We offer a [tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Alongside Brazil, Chile, Bolivia and Ecuador, it includes Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Colombia. The four highlighted countries are part of this larger programme, not a separate continuous route with only four stops.

The journey combines historical excursions with nature-focused stages. Bolivia's lagoons and the Galápagos, for example, are primarily about scenery and wildlife. The cultural content should therefore be assessed by examining individual days rather than counting the countries.

## Brazil: Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and Rio's historic quarters

In [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the programme includes a trip up Corcovado to the Christ the Redeemer statue and a separate sightseeing day covering Sugarloaf Mountain and the old city. The urban route takes in churches, monasteries and buildings from the colonial period.

This is Brazil's cultural section, where a modern city sits alongside familiar twentieth-century icons and older architecture. These are sightseeing excursions rather than a comprehensive exploration of every museum in Rio. The visit to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) focuses on waterfalls and should not be presented as an additional history-focused stage.

If Brazil's history is your main interest, explore [cultural tours in Brazil](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/).

## Chile: Santiago's historic centre before the highlands

In [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), a sightseeing excursion with a Russian-speaking guide is included. It introduces the old city and its principal public spaces. This historical section naturally precedes the flight to Calama and transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/).

On this tour, the Atacama is primarily a place to experience natural landscapes and prepare for Bolivia's high elevations. Its activities should not be confused with a tour of Santiago's historic districts. That is one of the trade-offs of a lengthy itinerary: some days are devoted to travel and changes between climate zones.

## Bolivia: Tiwanaku as a cultural destination in its own right

In Bolivia, after the high-altitude lagoons, salt flats and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the route passes through [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). It then continues to [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and on towards the Peruvian border. This ancient archaeological complex reveals tangible traces of a civilisation that existed in the Andes before the Incas.

Tiwanaku is the most clearly defined archaeological site on the Bolivian section of the programme. It deserves particular attention if you are choosing the tour for its history. Yet the excursion forms part of the day spent crossing into Peru: time at the site is not equivalent to an additional full day of archaeological exploration. If you want a more leisurely visit, discuss it when planning a private itinerary.

## Ecuador: Quito and the equator, followed by a different kind of journey

The Ecuadorian section starts in Quito. A city sightseeing day includes sites associated with the equator line. The page about [Quito and Cotopaxi Volcano](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/) helps explain the region's geography, but its title does not mean that an excursion to Cotopaxi Volcano is included on this particular day.

Later, travellers head to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). Island and sea excursions follow, with nature taking centre stage. For culture enthusiasts, this provides contrast but does not replace historical trips on mainland Ecuador.

## What to consider when choosing a culture-focused journey

Each country has a different emphasis. Brazil offers Rio's urban landmarks; Chile, Santiago; Bolivia, Tiwanaku; and Ecuador, Quito and the equator. Between these experiences lies an extensive nature programme, including elevations over 4,000 metres, salt flats and islands.

If your goal is to spend as many days as possible in museums and archaeological sites, a long eight-country journey may be too broad. If you want to see how cities, natural environments and historical heritage change across South America in one trip, the combination makes sense. Check the programme and conditions on the [specific tour page](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

For a narrower choice, browse [cultural and historical tours in Bolivia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/bolivia/) and [cultural journeys in Ecuador](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/ecuador/). [All culture-focused multi-country itineraries](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) offer other combinations, while the [general catalogue for these four countries](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_ecuador/) displays them without a thematic filter.

## Frequently asked questions about the cultural programme

### Is Tiwanaku included?

Yes. Travelling via Tiwanaku forms part of the approved route from La Paz towards Peru.

### Are there dedicated museum days in every country?

No. The cultural activities are spread unevenly: Brazil and Chile feature city sightseeing, Bolivia an archaeological site, and Ecuador Quito and the equator line. Nature excursions are scheduled between them.

### Do I have to visit the four countries in this exact order?

Our tour follows its own sequence through eight countries. Selecting these four does not change the order of the entire journey. A different travel sequence requires a separately agreed itinerary.

## From Brazil's waterfalls to the Galápagos: how the route works

The natural landscapes of [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/), [Bolivia](/bolivia/) and [Ecuador](/ecuador/) could hardly be more different. Brazil's Iguazu is memorable for its powerful cascades and humid forests. Chile's Atacama reveals dry, high-altitude expanses. Bolivia's lagoons and salt flats reflect the geological and volcanic processes of the Andes, while the Galápagos Islands demonstrate how the archipelago's isolation shaped the development of its plant and animal life.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. [Ada Tours' “Eight South American countries in 32 days” programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) visits all these natural regions, but also travels through Argentina, Uruguay, Peru and Colombia. The four-country combination in this page's title is a geographical filter, not a separate four-country offer with its own price. The general selection without a thematic restriction is here: [Bolivia + Brazil + Chile + Ecuador](/multi-country/bolivia_brazil_chile_ecuador/).

The strength of the complete programme is the chance to experience three fundamentally different environments for nature excursions: humid forests, cold highlands and oceanic islands. When choosing, account for the transitions between them: the South American route involves flights, bus journeys and a two-day trip in off-road vehicles.

## Brazil: Rio's panoramas and Iguazu Falls

At the beginning of the journey, you arrive in São Paulo and then travel to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Excursions to Corcovado, the Christ the Redeemer statue and Sugarloaf Mountain reveal the mountainous shape of the coastline and the urban landscape. These panoramic excursions do not turn the programme into a trek through Tijuca Forest: no separate multi-day hike there is listed.

The highlight of Brazil's natural scenery is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). A Russian-speaking guide accompanies the excursion to the Brazilian side, where pathways provide sweeping views of the falls. The Argentine side of Iguazu is also included in the full programme, although it belongs to another country outside the four highlighted here.

It is especially important to distinguish included activities from optional ones. On the current tour, the Bird Park and Macuco Safari boat excursion are listed at an additional cost. If birdwatching or approaching the waterfalls from the water is a priority, arrange these options separately. The walk through the national park itself already offers views of the waterfall system and surrounding forest.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama and preparation for altitude

The next nature-focused section begins after the city visits in Argentina, Uruguay and Santiago. You fly to Calama and travel to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The dry air, sunny days and cold nights here are very different from the humid conditions at Iguazu.

In the current programme, San Pedro is primarily an overnight stop and a place to prepare for the road across the high-altitude border. A night-time astronomy excursion is offered as an extra, subject to the lunar calendar; it is not automatically included in the standard activities. Being in the Atacama also does not mean that all the famous lakes, lagoons and dunes around San Pedro are included. Assess the activities for this specific day against the approved programme.

Next, you cross the border between Chile and Bolivia and begin the expedition section in four-wheel-drive vehicles. This transition involves a change of transport and altitude. Its planning must account for actual road conditions, the weather and the group's ability to acclimatise.

## Bolivia: Laguna Verde, Sol de Mañana and Uyuni

On the first day of the Bolivian jeep route, the group visits [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) and Licancabur Volcano, passing through the Dalí Desert and Polques springs and the Sol de Mañana area towards Laguna Colorada. Open high-altitude landscapes, mineral-rich lakes and geothermal activity contrast sharply with Brazil's coastline. The group spends the night in an expedition-style hotel.

On the second day, the programme continues through the Honda, Chiar Khota, Hedionda and Cañapa lagoons, the Ollagüe Volcano area and the Chiguana salt flat towards [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Stops along the way include Colchani, the “Eye of Water” and an island with large cacti. A packed lunch is included. The important point is that the itinerary visits **several distinct natural sights**, rather than treating the entire day as one photo opportunity on the salt flat.

Uyuni's mirror effect depends on surface water and weather conditions. In dry conditions, the experience can be quite different: a white salt surface, geometric patterns and an immense horizon. The expedition route depends on access to particular roads and natural conditions; no specific appearance of the salt flat can be guaranteed for a given date.

After Uyuni, you continue by plane to La Paz and visit the Valley of the Moon. The route then passes through Tiwanaku towards Lake Titicaca in Peru, where the next stage of the complete eight-country journey begins.

## Andean altitude: what to discuss beforehand

Parts of the Bolivian highland itinerary rise above 4,000 metres above sea level. Even if travellers spend much of the time in a vehicle, symptoms of altitude sickness can occur at that elevation. San Pedro de Atacama is included as an intermediate acclimatisation stop, but this does not eliminate individual risks.

On the practical side, clarify the duration and nature of the expedition drives, accommodation, meals, night-time temperatures and options for changing the route in bad weather. Travellers with relevant medical conditions should discuss a high-altitude journey with a doctor. Everyone will need warm clothing and protection from strong sun, wind and very dry air.

## Ecuador: Quito and the journey towards oceanic islands

After Peru, the group flies to [Quito](/ecuador/). The itinerary includes a day exploring the historic centre, the basilica, the Panecillo area, the Intiñan Museum and the Mitad del Mundo complex. Quito sits at considerable elevation; this is a day of city sightseeing and cultural visits, not an ascent of an Ecuadorian volcano.

The group then flies to the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The aircraft lands on Baltra; travellers cross the Itabaca Channel to [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and continue to Puerto Ayora. The programme includes a visit to the Santa Cruz highlands, where the landscape changes along the way from dry, rocky areas to the island's greener interior.

The Galápagos archipelago is inscribed on UNESCO's World Natural Heritage List. Its significance reflects its volcanic origins, long isolation and the development of its remarkable animal life. During the visit, follow national park rules and guide instructions, avoid approaching animals without permission and leave no litter. Sightings of specific species depend on landing sites, seasons and the behaviour of the animals themselves.

## A day at sea in the Galápagos: one of two alternatives

The programme offers **two mutually exclusive options** for one full day of sea excursions. The exact route is confirmed after booking; both alternatives are not included at the same time.

**Option 1: North Seymour and Bachas.** Travellers board a yacht for North Seymour, known for its coastal cliffs and seabird colonies. Frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies may be seen on the island when conditions allow. The journey then continues to Bachas Beach for a walk and snorkelling. The nature description of this option also mentions a coastal lagoon where flamingos are sometimes present.

**Option 2: South Plaza and Cape Carrión.** On South Plaza, the walk passes through volcanic terrain with vegetation, sea lions and land iguanas. After lunch on board, the boat continues to Cape Carrión for snorkelling. Seeing rays, sharks or fish underwater depends on the natural environment and sea conditions; no encounter with any particular species is guaranteed.

There are meaningful differences between the alternatives. The first is often chosen for North Seymour's bird colonies and Bachas Beach; the second appeals to those interested in South Plaza's land wildlife and the marine setting at Cape Carrión. However, the final choice depends on confirmation of the vessel, timetable and permits. Before choosing the tour, find out exactly which places are included in each option rather than expecting all four island stops in one day.

After the sea excursion, travellers return to their accommodation, then head to Baltra and fly to Guayaquil. The full itinerary continues to Colombia, which is part of the eight-country journey even though it does not appear in this thematic filter's title.

## Combining mountain climates with island weather

The route first passes through humid Iguazu, then the dry Atacama, Bolivia's cold highlands and finally the maritime climate of the Galápagos. Packing for all these conditions requires thought. In Bolivia, warm layers and wind protection are essential; on the islands, bring lightweight clothing, sun protection and gear for sea excursions, while near the falls you will need protection from spray.

Choosing dates for the Galápagos depends on the wildlife you want to see and ocean conditions; for Uyuni, it depends on the expected state of the salt flat. The most favourable conditions at these destinations may occur in different seasons. Thus, the “best month for four countries” depends on your priority: the reflective salt-flat surface, reliable travel conditions in the highlands or watching marine animals.

For the islands, also check the current rules on visiting protected areas, immigration procedures, biosecurity, applicable fees and guide requirements. Specific amounts and procedures can change; rely on official information before travelling rather than an old price list found by chance.

## Cost, flights and trip duration

The current programme lasts **32 days and 31 nights**. It describes 4-star hotels, domestic flights, transfers and excursions on the scheduled days. International flights are paid for separately. Russian-speaking guides accompany some excursions, while English-speaking guides are used for certain nature and sea excursions. Consider this when choosing the type of guiding you prefer.

The full programme starts at **$15 500 per person sharing a ½ DBL room**; the separate SGL rate is higher. That figure covers the approved itinerary through all eight countries. It is not possible to select only Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador and automatically retain the same price and services: different flight connections and a separate commercial proposal would be required.

For entry and transit, check the rules of all eight countries for the traveller's nationality and the way each border is crossed. It is also worth clarifying baggage restrictions on regional airlines and payment options in remote high-altitude areas. Ecuador uses the US dollar, while the other selected countries have their own currencies, so no universal payment method can be promised for the entire journey in advance.

## Choosing between the Galápagos and other nature destinations

If marine animals, endemic species and island ecology matter most, the Galápagos section will be the strongest argument for this trip. If you want to explore volcanic landscapes, salt, lagoons and geysers, the Chile–Bolivia route is likely to be more compelling. Iguazu Falls add even more variety to the sequence, although they lie much farther from the other natural attractions.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Bolivia, Brazil, Chile and Ecuador

### Can I visit Iguazu, Uyuni and the Galápagos in one tour?

Yes. All three destinations are included in [Ada Tours' 32-day programme](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Other countries, excursions and flights are scheduled between them.

### Can I visit North Seymour and South Plaza on the same day?

Not on the published itinerary. The sea excursion follows one of two alternatives: North Seymour with Bachas, or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. The chosen option is confirmed after booking.

### Do I need mountain-hiking experience for Uyuni?

The two-day journey takes place mainly in off-road vehicles, but many stops are above 4,000 metres. Altitude itself places demands on the body, so personal health and acclimatisation must be taken into account.

### Is the Atacama astronomy excursion included in the price?

No. It is listed as optional and takes place only when conditions are suitable and the excursion has been confirmed.

### Does the Galápagos section guarantee giant tortoise sightings?

No such guarantee is given. Visiting the Santa Cruz highlands and taking the sea excursion provide opportunities to observe wildlife, but actual encounters depend on the selected route and natural circumstances.
